data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only if the test's guard conditions are installed as part of the subject's runtime environment rather than as independent observers, and the 3-of-26 result is the fraction of mutations that were invisible to guards installed under shown-to-fail-first conditions.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If all guards were installed identically across all modules regardless of shown-to-fail-first state, then the installation-order mechanism is not the cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation lost under compile.py was in an ordinarily-guarded module and not in a special installation path, then the distribution is unexplained.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a re-run with guards installed before any failure is shown still loses the same mutation, then the constraint is elsewhere.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The ordinarily-guarded modules (4/4 to 6/7) had guards that were active during normal execution. The one mutation lost under compile.py was in a location where the guard was not installed until after the failure had already been shown. The test thus constrained the subject by making the guard's presence conditional on the failure's prior visibility, creating a circular dependency: the test only catches mutations that do not change what the installation procedure already revealed. The 3-of-26 distribution reflects the number of mutations whose detection depended on guards that were installed after the failure was exposed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
